title: easement.yml
description: Configuration of the easement architecture quality gate.

accept_augmentations.description: Accept implicit module-string relationships to exactly one augmentation file, for the listed consumers. Direct imports and explicit symbol uses remain checked.

baseline.description: Path of the baseline file, default easement.baseline.yml.

common.description: Components every other component may depend on.

components.description: Named parts of the system and the paths they cover.

diagram.description: A Markdown file with a Mermaid graph or flowchart of the components (or a .mmd file). A dependency between components the diagram has no arrow for fails as diagram. Nodes match components by id or label.

entry.description: Files the program starts from (cmd/**, src/main.ts). With it, a checked file of a component that no chain of imports from them, from a test or from a file of no component reaches fails as unused. A language whose import graph misses uses is not judged, and the report says so.

examples.description: Policy examples: proposed dependencies with the decision each must get, judged by every `check` without any code that imports them. One that gets another decision fails as `example` at its line, so a later grant cannot silently undo a prohibition. Paths are relative to the root and need not exist; a source or a target path no component owns cannot be judged and fails. `extends` joins the lists.

extends.description: Config files merged underneath this one, relative to this file. Patterns stay relative to the root of the config being loaded.

forbid_symbol.description: Names that no checked file may use, components and files that belong to none alike, as `package.Name` or `import/path.Name`, a member after its type (`ent.Client.Query`). A component's own `forbid_symbol` adds to it. An item may carry its own reason, and `allow`: the components that may use the name all the same.

indexers.description: Settings of an indexer, by the language it reads: `go: { tags: [race] }` indexes Go files behind `//go:build race` too (files behind other tags are not built, so they count as not covered). An unknown language or setting fails.

layers.description: Components from the top layer to the bottom one: a layer may depend on any layer below it, never on one above. A list in place of a name holds sibling components of one layer, which do not depend on each other; {name, closed: true} is a layer the ones above cannot reach past.

manifests.description: Every external module a file imports has to be a dependency of the nearest package.json, go.mod or Cargo.toml above it, else it fails as undeclared. Other languages are not checked.

no_cycles.description: Fail on dependency cycles between components: true for all, or a list of components.

packages.description: Manifests are checked files: each dependency a `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` or `go.mod` declares is a dependency of the component that owns it, on a package of the project or on an external module, so the rules apply to it. A dev-dependency is test code, which `tests: auto` takes. Other manifests are not read yet.

reach.description: What `must_not_reach` follows: `files` (the default) takes an import for everything its file imports; `symbols` follows the definitions a call references, so calling one pure method does not reach what another method of its file uses. A file the index gave no ranges keeps reaching as a whole.

rules.description: Per component: what it may depend on and use.

strict.description: Fail on checked files that belong to no component, except those matching `unowned`.

target_only.description: Globs of files (generated code) that stay in the graph as targets, so components can own them and rules can allow or forbid importing them, but are never checked as the source of a dependency. `exclude` wins over it.

tests.description: `auto` puts the test files of every language (`*_test.go`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`, `*Test.java`, …) into a component named `tests`, which `rules.tests` can restrict. Without such a rule tests may import anything.

uncovered_ok.description: Source files that no indexer covers and that may stay that way (globs, each with the reason). Others are listed in the report as not covered, and the result is marked partial.

unowned.description: Globs of files and directories that may belong to no component in strict mode.

warn.description: Rules whose violations are reported as warnings and do not fail the check. Rules about the config, such as unmatched, cannot be listed.

^x-.description: Free keys that only hold YAML anchors: `x-ban: &ban {...}`, then `<<: *ban` in a rule.

Accepted.description: An `uncovered_ok` entry: a glob, or `name` with one glob or a list of them that share a reason.

because.description: Why the files may stay uncovered, reported with the files it accepts.

name.description: A glob or a list of globs.

AugmentationAcceptance.description: An intentional implicit relationship to an external-module augmentation.

allow_importers.description: When set, only these components (and the component itself) may import it.

because.description: Why the public surface or the importer list exists; shown with their violations.

defines.description: Globs of type names that belong in this component (*Repository): a class, struct, interface or trait so named that another component defines fails as naming. Types are read from the index; files no index reads are an evidence gap.

except.description: Files matching these patterns do not belong to this component, even though `in` matches them.

in.description: A glob or a list of globs naming a module: a directory or a file. A named placeholder such as <feature> matches one directory like *, and both ends of an import that name it must fill it the same way.

isolated.description: The directories matched by `in` (each pattern needs a `*`, no `**`) are instances that must not import each other.

optional.description: The component may match no file. Otherwise an `in` pattern that matches no file of the project fails as `unmatched`. Default false.

owner.description: Who to ask about the component and its rules: a team or a person. Printed with the violations of the component.

part.description: With `packages`, the part of the files `in` matches that the component owns, as the language or manifest names it: `feature/fake` for the Cargo feature `fake`. The file itself stays with the component that has no `part`.

priority.description: Which component wins when several match a file: the higher priority, then the longer pattern. Default 0.

public.description: When set, other components may import only these paths.

public_symbols.description: When set, other components may use only these names from this component's packages. In a language whose uses of names easement does not read, the report has a `symbols` evidence gap instead.

surfaces.description: Named surfaces: paths of the component open only to the components each lists. With surfaces and no `public`, the public surface is empty.

Example.description: A policy example: a proposed dependency and the decision it must get.

because.description: Why the policy must decide so; shown when it does not.

external.description: The external module it would import; or `to`.

from.description: The file that would hold the import.

rule.description: The rule that must reject it, when the reason matters; without it any rejection satisfies `rejected`.

to.description: The path it would import; or `external`.

ExampleRule.description: The rules that can reject one dependency, and so a policy example.

Expect.description: The decision a policy example must get.

ForbiddenName.description: A name in a `forbid_symbol` list: a plain name, or one with a reason of its own and, at the top level, the components that may use it all the same.

allow.description: Only in the top-level `forbid_symbol`: the components that may use the name. Every other use is a violation, in the component that defines the name too.

because.description: Why this name is forbidden; shown instead of the reason of the whole rule.

Layer.description: One layer of `layers`: a component, sibling components that do not depend on each other, or a closed component that the layers above it cannot reach past.

Listed.description: A name in a rule's list, optionally with a reason of its own that is shown instead of the reason of the whole rule.

closed.description: The layers above may not reach past this one.

because.description: Why this item is listed; shown instead of the reason of the whole rule.
Why the rule exists; shown with its violations.

forbid_external.description: External modules this component must not use. $std stands for the standard library of the importing file's language. An item may carry its own reason.

forbid_file.description: File names or globs that no file of this component may match. An item may carry its own reason.

forbid_symbol.description: Names this component must not use, as `package.Name` or `import/path.Name` (`ent.Client`), a member after its type (`ent.Client.Query`). In a language whose uses of names easement does not read, the report has a `symbols` evidence gap instead. An item may carry its own reason.

max_fan_out.description: Most components this one may depend on.

max_instability.description: Highest instability, out / (in + out), from 0 (stable) to 1.

may_depend_on.description: Components this one may depend on. An item may carry its own reason, shown by `explain`.

may_use_external.description: External modules this component may use; unset means no restriction. A pattern covers submodules: lodash covers lodash/fp. $std stands for the standard library of the importing file's language. An item may carry its own reason.

must_depend_on.description: Components that every directory of this component must import at least once. An item may carry its own reason.

must_not_depend_on.description: Components that are never allowed, even if common or layers would allow them. An item may carry its own reason.

must_not_reach.description: Components this component must not depend on, directly or through any chain of imports, even when every hop is allowed. An item may carry its own reason.

must_use_external.description: External modules that every directory of this component must use; a pattern covers submodules. An item may carry its own reason.

requires_directive.description: Regular expressions that some file in every directory of this component must match, for dependencies written as comments (`//go:embed`, `goverter:converter`). An item may carry its own reason.

requires_file.description: File names or globs that every directory of this component must contain. An item may carry its own reason.

Surface.description: A named surface: paths of a component that only the listed components may import.

because.description: Why the surface exists; shown with its violations.

importers.description: The components that may import these paths; each must be in `allow_importers` when the component has one.

in.description: A glob or a list of globs inside the component, naming a module as `public` does.
